current.summary: Same S4 three-summand family on the a=-3 deployed shape (P-256 and GOST CryptoPro-B classes, generic j, no CM), now decided by an **S3-anchored pair sweep** instead of the S4 quartic + Cantor-Zassenhaus: for each factor-base anchor F_i and both signs form R' = R -+ F_i, then two-decompose R' by solving the quadratic S3(x_j, X, x_R') = 0 for every x_j in the base -- one quadratic and one square root per candidate instead of a quartic plus a full X^p mod f and equal-degree splitting. The family is not approximated: s3_anchor_sweep_matches_the_quartic_triple_census checks both oracles against a brute-force sign census on the 16-bit rung (anchored set equals the census exactly; the CZ set is a subset that contains the planted triple), and every row is re-added in the group before use. Ladder at 16/20/24/28 bits with fb=120: median trials/relation 1.0 (16), 1.0 (20), 6.0 (24), 72.5 (28); median per-relation wall 0.145 ms (16), 3.791 ms (20), 113.956 ms (24), 1994.122 ms (28). The 28-bit rungs (p=268435399 p256 class, p=268435361 CryptoPro-B class) are the first of this family past 24 bits. A paired single-seed 16-bit run measured 291.532 s for the quartic/CZ oracle and 0.0185 s for the anchored sweep on the same 128 relations. At 28 bits the anchored 3-decomposition (245-390 s) is within about 2x of the current-tree 2-decomposition driver on the same fixtures (121-167 s for 128 rows), which needs one fewer column per row. FFD inapplicable with reason (direct univariate root finding; no GB/SAT system). Constant factor only: the anchored sweep still costs ~p*c per relation-search pass, so this does not move the vs_rho frontier.

next_target.summary: Extend the anchored sweep to 32 bits under the same policy, and cut the per-candidate cost further (u64 inner loop for p < 2^63, batch inversion of the 2B anchor slopes) so a larger factor base is affordable: the density p/B^3 is still the lever, and the open measurement is the B at which 3-decomposition total wall meets 2-decomposition total wall.

history.summary: First Semaev-S4 3-decomposition relation family past toy sizes on the deployed a=-3 curve shape (P-256 class, 16-bit prime p=65519): relations decompose R = aG + bQ into three factor-base points via the S4 quartic + Cantor-Zassenhaus root finding (find_roots_fp_fast); measured trials/relation = 1.0 (every trial yields a relation; ~13 expected hits/trial at fb=120), 128 relations, staged timers, known-answer verified and rho-agreeing. Per-relation wall 3.3 s is dominated by the B^2/2 quartic sweep at fixed B=120, so 2-decomposition remains faster per relation at these sizes; the confirmed p/B^3 3-decomposition density is the input for the larger-B design where 3-decomposition is the asymptotic lever.
